rubric_items.done_when: pass — §7's done-when now carries a measurable floor (every shot's boundary RMS against SELENE under 0.10 m) and a declared must-fail control (the same run with loop 7's `channel_factor` flipped to +1 stamps a larger whitened magnetics residual on every shot), and §6's names a hand-computed factor per unit pair, so both gates can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the staged map copies land under `~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/imas-ambix/maps-staging/<node>` and the live bundle under `/work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/maps`, both durable, with no node-local temporary path named as an evidence store.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no ticket numbers, stage names or version tags reach the symbols or comments; the `jtmm-*` identifiers are the plan's own node vocabulary and the physics shorthand (OP1/OP2, E101154, PSRC) names the machine, not a plan item.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — I applied all three checks: the §6 root-cause chain (one-turn prediction, then the double-counted filament factor) matches its own cited measurements (fragment `jtmm-vacuum-mismatch-rca`, merge 8a873b69) and the corrected slope −14 → −0.40; each section's stated mechanism (the vacuum operator, the sign kernel, the machine-keyed pin table) is capable of producing its done-when; and the mechanisms name their real callers (`ForwardOperator.assemble_pf_currents` reached by `build_operator`, `ArtifactMachineSelector` as the sole production constructor), so no mechanism runs unreached.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each named node carries one deliverable (for example `jtmm-fame-equilibrium-map` authors one map, `jtmm-sign-cohort` makes one reader argument optional), so each closes on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the s6→s7 dependency and the `conventions-before-equilibrium` gate that holds §7 on §6's sign report resolve; §7's gate names `data-section="s7" data-gated-sections="s7"` and no declared relationship points at the wrong node.
